solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go, but only pay the minimum?

definitions.meaning: a British euphemism for going to the toilet, from the old coin-operated public lavatory locks
to part with the smallest coin there is, a single penny

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to leave while paying as little as they can get away with.
explanation.walkthrough: British public toilets once cost a penny to use, hence the euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic British euphemism for urinating, literally laying out one penny, the smallest sum.

clue.text: Help politician to pocket billions? A sorry tale

indicators.note: to pocket is to take something inside, so the help-and-politician string holds the billions letter within it

parts.note: SOS is the distress call asking for help
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician helps himself to billions, and it ends in a sad story of excuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help' is the distress call, not assistance; 'to pocket' makes the politician's string hold the billions inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-luck account told to win sympathy is exactly a sorry tale.

clue.text: Happy about first lady almost getting high

indicators.note: about means around, so the happy word goes round the shortened name

parts.note: elated means joyful, happy

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A cheerful first lady who is nearly getting high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' shortens the first lady by a letter; 'about' wraps the happy word round her.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: raised up, lofty, as in a raised platform or position.

clue.text: Day heading for disaster? Boris blows top

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so take the start of disaster
losing one's top here means the name sheds its first letter

explanation.surface: On a day heading for disaster, Boris Johnson loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boris blows top' sounds like the British politician Boris Johnson losing his temper; it actually removes his initial B.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer and actress Doris Day, so her surname alone points to her first name.

clue.text: Show rotten English poet up

indicators.note: rotten means bad or spoilt, so these letters are in poor order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A bad English poet is put on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep out is to appear briefly or partly, to become visible.

clue.text: Book revealing unusual case of Libya

parts.note: novel means new and unusual

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A book that exposes a strange affair involving Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: A short novel is a kind of book, longer than a short story.

clue.text: Starry-eyed Romeo leaving in distress not long ago

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the Romeo letter departs from the starry-eyed letters
in distress means troubled and disordered, so the remaining letters are scrambled

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dreamy Romeo goes off in a state of distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes one R from STARRYEYED, and 'in distress' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today, or loosely in the recent past, is a time not long ago.

clue.text: Cut price lettuce

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the price word loses its tail letter

parts.note: cost is another word for price

explanation.surface: A cheap lettuce on discount at the greengrocer's.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of lettuce, also called romaine.

clue.text: My privates? Her Majesty's always fondling them

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
GIs are US enlisted soldiers, privates

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast that the Queen is forever touching one's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, not a possessive, and 'privates' are soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II kept and was constantly petting her dogs, a breed of Welsh herding dog.

clue.text: Something that exhausts a soldier?

definitions.meaning: one that saps strength or drains, read literally
a military engineer, especially in the British army

explanation.surface: Asks what wears out a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A military engineer digging trenches, and literally one who drains energy.

clue.text: Sing thus and yell, half-cut in boozer

indicators.note: in places the halved yell inside the pub word

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, a bar

indicators.note: half-cut cuts the word in half, keeping its first two letters; it is also British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy in the pub sings and yells along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, fitting the pub, but here it halves YELL to YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing without written music, relying on hearing, is doing it this way.

clue.text: Listen as Cockney retches by sink

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the H sound at the start of words

parts.note: heaves means retches, as in being sick
drop and sink both mean fall

explanation.surface: An East Londoner being sick over the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner; their accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen secretly to others' private conversation.

clue.text: Lowlifes wanting money back? It makes you sick

parts.note: toads are contemptible people, lowlifes

indicators.note: back means the money word is read backwards

parts.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: Crooks who want their money returned, and find it sickening.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous fungus that can make a person ill if eaten.

clue.text: Priest beginning to take ecstasy and crack

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

indicators.note: the beginning of the word take is its first letter

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A priest who starts taking ecstasy and crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like the drug next to ecstasy, but it is the adjective meaning first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: As in crack troops: best, top-quality, select.

clue.text: Look longingly round European court and return to office

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the looking word reverses

parts.note: to leer is to look with longing or lust

explanation.surface: Someone gazes around a European court, then goes back to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting someone back in puts them back into their position, restoring them to office.

clue.text: One of us needing another large hint

indicators.note: another means a different version, so the letters are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A person who needs a second, bigger clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A human being, an inhabitant of our planet, as opposed to aliens.

clue.text: Reckons theologian's in the way

indicators.note: in places the theologian inside the way word

parts.note: as means in the way that, as in 'do as I do'
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A theologian standing in the road makes calculations.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to reckon or tot up is to sum figures.

clue.text: Nightclub performer, one falling under bus in the end

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed after
the end of the word bus is its final letter

parts.note: a tripper is one who trips and falls

explanation.surface: A club dancer who ends up tumbling beneath a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who undresses on stage, typically at a nightclub.

clue.text: I was mistaken about books being buried

indicators.note: about means around, so the mistaken phrase goes round the books

parts.note: erred means made a mistake
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone admits being wrong about books that were buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed in a grave, laid to rest underground.

clue.text: King sunk in gloom — he'll probably croak

indicators.note: sunk in means buried inside, so the king letter goes into the gloom word

parts.note: fog is murk, darkness, gloom
R is from Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A depressed monarch who looks likely to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'croak' suggests dying, but it means the noise this animal makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal's call is a croak, so it is the creature most likely to make it.

clue.text: Stupidly goes round to bug police

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the bug word
stupidly means done in a muddled way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to tap a phone is to bug it

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly calls round to plant a listening device for the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupidly' gives GESO, and 'round' wraps it about the bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi secret police force of the Third Reich.

clue.text: Attempt to seduce? One might with item from Ann Summers

definitions.meaning: British slang for making a cheeky pass at someone

definitions.text: One might with item from Ann Summers
definitions.meaning: Ann Summers is a British chain of lingerie shops, so a customer would test a garment for fit

explanation.surface: A seduction attempt aided by lingerie bought at a high-street sex shop.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom for chancing a move, and literally putting on a garment to check fit.

clue.text: Exploit customers at work

parts.note: a business's trade is its customers
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of shoppers while on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To profit from or take advantage of something, such as a reputation.

clue.text: Cries when wife rings?

parts.note: hoops are rings

explanation.surface: Shouts heard whenever a wife phones.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts of joy or excitement, as plural nouns.

clue.text: Kit that you might need for car, I hear

indicators.note: I hear signals that the word is spoken and only its sound counts

parts.words: that you might need for car
parts.note: a car needs a tyre, one rubber wheel covering

explanation.surface: Equipment that a driver might need.
explanation.walkthrough: TYRE is the British spelling of tire.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit means clothing or outfit, as in sports kit.

clue.text: Husband's lust a problem?

parts.note: an itch is a restless desire, a lust

explanation.surface: Asks whether a husband's desire is causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or difficulty, as in 'without a hitch'.

clue.text: Something spicy, such as Sun article I briefly see

parts.note: the Sun is an example of a star
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word see loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A spicy story in The Sun tabloid, glanced at quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the British tabloid newspaper, but is the star.
explanation.definitionFit: A star-shaped Chinese spice with an aniseed flavour.

clue.text: Agree Johnson finally must go? That would be a blessing

indicators.note: must go means is to be removed, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: to assent is to agree

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of Johnson

explanation.surface: Agreeing Boris Johnson must finally resign would be a relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valuable or useful, a boon or blessing.

clue.text: Begin to hold forth about island tipple

indicators.note: about means around, so the speech word goes round island and drink

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech, hold forth
gin is a drink, a tipple

explanation.surface: Someone starts lecturing about a favourite island drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To start or arise, to come into being.

clue.text: Very nice meal. 1p off

indicators.note: off means removed, so the penny letter is taken out

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
one penny is written 1p, P being the British abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A lovely meal, with a penny knocked off the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: excellent, great.

clue.text: Woman knocking back some chartreuse

indicators.note: knocking back means the found letters are read backwards; it also means drinking
some means part of the word, so letters are found within chartreuse

explanation.surface: A woman downing a glass of chartreuse liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Friendly don outraged when sacked

indicators.note: sacked means plundered and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university don is furious after being fired, yet stays friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' seems to mean fired, but it signals plunder and disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: kindly, amiable and pleasant in temperament.
